title: paper_v2 config_change_audit.change_type semantics — action vs subject split follow-up
description: Round-2 fix renamed CHECK constraint ck_paper_v2_config_change_audit_type → ck_..._action and changed enum from subject-type (runtime_profile/execution_policy/.../other) to action-type (CREATE/ACTIVATE/DEACTIVATE/MODIFY) to match live source. Source column is misleadingly named change_type but actually carries action info. Subject info lives in old_value_json/new_value_json payload. Follow-up question: should archive split into action_type + subject_type two columns for queryability (avoid JSON path queries for subject)? Deferred design decision. Source actual values: CREATE 96, ACTIVATE 136 (only 2 seen so far).
reproduce_command: psql -h 127.0.0.1 -p 5433 -d aistock -c "SELECT change_type, count(*) FROM paper_v2.config_change_audit GROUP BY 1"
required_verification: Future query pattern review with stakeholders
If split decided: migration adds subject_type column + handler populates from JSON
closure_requirements: Decision recorded: keep single action column vs split action+subject

events.note: Round-2 P1.4 audit fixed semantic but flagged split as deferred design pass
Linked BUG-010 to GitHub Issue #321 for standard workflow tracking.
Recorded that change_type remains the source action enum and subject/category queries must inspect JSON payloads unless a future migration adds subject_type.

validation_evidence: No SQL or handler code change required; existing handler and SQL already enforce source action enum CREATE/ACTIVATE/DEACTIVATE/MODIFY.
